chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said:
There is no believer who lets his brother down when he is capable of supporting him, except that God lets him down in this world and the Hereafter.

key_terms.مُؤْمِن: mu'min — a true believer, one who has genuine faith, used here to emphasize that abandonment is incompatible with true faith
key_terms.نُصْرَة: nusrah — active support, assistance, coming to someone's aid when they need help
key_terms.يَخْذُلُ: letting down/abandoning — khidhlān refers to withdrawing support and leaving someone vulnerable, the opposite of nusrah (aid)

ai.seo_question: What happens to a Muslim who refuses to help his brother when capable?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) declares that abandoning a fellow believer when one has the capacity to help is a grave moral failing that results in divine abandonment in both this life and the next. This teaching addresses the essential bonds of mutual solidarity in the Muslim community — the Imam spoke to a society where believers faced persecution, making communal support a matter of survival and religious duty. The divine consequence — being abandoned by God — mirrors the moral violation, establishing a principle of reciprocal neglect as divine justice.
